issues.description: The problem statement is internally inconsistent about the type of the Farm.animals attribute: the UML diagram declares animals: List<Animal> while the textual Part 3 explicitly requires using a Set implemented with HashSet. This contradiction can confuse students which collection type to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction in the problem statement: either update the UML to show animals: Set<Animal> (HashSet) to match the textual requirement, or change the textual description to require a List if the UML is intended. Prefer documenting animals as Set<Animal> in UML and text if uniqueness is required.

issues.description: The provided solution implements Farm.animals as a List<Animal> (ArrayList) rather than the Set/HashSet required by the textual specification in Part 3; this also fails to enforce the uniqueness constraint described in the task. Students following the solution or template may be misled and produce implementations that allow duplicates.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the solution (and template) to use a Set<Animal> (e.g. private Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>();) and update the getter/setter signatures accordingly. Ensure addAnimal adds to the Set and feedAllAnimals iterates over the Set. Alternatively, if a List is intended, update the problem text to remove the uniqueness/HashSet requirement so all artifacts are consistent.

issues.description: The collection used to represent the farm's animals is referenced with different type identifiers across artifacts: the UML fragment in the problem statement shows animals: List<Animal> while the textual task description requires a Set implemented via HashSet (to guarantee uniqueness). The solution implements animals as a List/ArrayList. This mismatch (List vs Set/HashSet) creates confusion about the intended data structure and the requirement to prevent duplicates.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification and implementation: either (A) update the problem statement and UML to require a List/ArrayList if duplicates are acceptable, or (B) change the template and solution to use Set<Animal> animals and initialize it with new HashSet<>(), updating getters/setters and any code that depends on List methods. Prefer option B to preserve the explicit textual requirement for unique animals.
